summary: This two-center prospective cohort study from Russia assessed respiratory outcomes and treatment of broncho-obstructive syndrome (BOS) in 10,456 post-COVID-19 patients. In the treatment comparison (n=7,497 with BOS), extra-fine beclomethasone dipropionate/formoterol (EMD BDP/FORM) in MART mode was superior to nebulized budesonide plus salbutamol at 24 weeks, with significantly better ACQ-5 scores and fewer as-needed inhaler uses (p<0.05), particularly in patients with eosinophils ≥150 cells/mcL. In a separate cohort of 89 patients with moderate-to-severe COVID-19, DLCO remained impaired in 94% at 6 months and 85% at 12 months, with severe disease, ICU admission, and high-flow oxygen therapy identified as risk factors for persistent DLCO reduction.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This paper presents TWO distinct study populations: (1) Center 1 (n=10,456) for BOS treatment comparison between EMD BDP/FORM (n=3,245) and nebulized budesonide+salbutamol (n=4,252) — note these are both within the 7,497 BOS subgroup, and further split into 4 subgroups by eosinophil level and COVID severity; (2) Center 2 UNIF (n=89) for longitudinal DLCO/pulmonary function follow-up at 6 and 12 months comparing moderate (n=49) vs severe (n=40) COVID-19. Outcomes 1-4 pertain to Center 1 treatment groups; outcomes 5-7 pertain to Center 2 observational groups. The arm_ids 3 and 4 are used for Center 2 moderate and severe COVID-19 groups respectively, as this is a distinct sub-study. Per-arm means in Table 2 are reported as M±m (mean±SE, not SD) per the statistical methods section. The total arm 1 n=3,245 and arm 2 n=4,252 — these include all subgroups; the treatment outcomes are reported for n=974 newly diagnosed asthma patients specifically at treatment period 3 (weeks 8-24). Some figures referenced (Figs 3 and 4) show DLCO vs ICU/high-flow oxygen correlations but no extractable numeric values are provided in text.

summary: This open-label quasi-experimental study from Russia compared a 21-day inpatient/outpatient multimodal pulmonary rehabilitation program (physiotherapy, haloinhilation, nebulizer therapy, exercise) versus no rehabilitation in 34 patients with pre-existing bronchoobstructive disease (asthma or COPD) who had recovered from COVID-19 pneumonia. At 3 months, the rehabilitation group showed significantly greater reductions in CT lung involvement (43.5% to 16% vs 39.6% to 37.8%), improvements in VC and FEV1 (1.5-fold increase, p<0.001), reduced mMRC dyspnea (−0.65 points, p<0.001), lower CAT scores, reduced inflammatory markers (CRP −24%, leukocytes reduced 2.4-fold), and lower pulmonary fibrosis prevalence (16% vs 31% at 3 months). The comparison group showed no clinically meaningful improvement or slight worsening on most measures. These results should be interpreted cautiously given non-random group allocation and lack of statistical adjustment for baseline differences.

summary: This prospective 4-arm cohort study (n=113) conducted in Russia compared a respiratory rehabilitation program including aquatic training (main group, n=25) versus no rehabilitation (n=25), Eastern medicine methods (n=29), or balneotherapy/physiotherapy (n=34) in post-COVID syndrome patients over 6 months of follow-up via structured telephone interview. The main group had significantly lower rates of GP consultations than all comparison groups (p=0.001 for all) and significantly lower hospitalization rates versus the no-rehabilitation group (4% vs 28%, RR=0.143, 95% CI 0.1–1.0, p=0.021), though hospitalization differences versus the Eastern medicine and balneotherapy groups did not reach statistical significance. The respiratory rehabilitation program showed the largest reduction in relative risk of hospitalization (85.7% vs no rehabilitation, 66.0% vs balneotherapy, 42.0% vs Eastern medicine), suggesting sustained preventive benefits over 6 months post-treatment.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Paper is in Russian with English abstract. No continuous/scale outcome data reported — study focuses exclusively on healthcare utilization (binary) endpoints at a single 6-month follow-up timepoint. No baseline per-arm demographics reported (only overall sample: mean age 58.4, 73.45% female, median age Q1-Q3 48-70). Groups were stated to be comparable on sex, age, and rehabilitation routing scale but no per-arm values provided. Chi-square statistics for hospitalization comparisons reported as chi2=5.357 p=0.021 (arm1 vs arm2), chi2=0.125 p=0.724 (arm1 vs arm3), chi2=0.856 p=0.355 (arm1 vs arm4). Table note indicates chi2 was not applicable for some cells (zero events), which limits statistical interpretation of pulmonologist and EMS outcomes. The study was nested within a larger RCT but uses observational cohort design for this sub-study. Overall time since infection at enrollment was 6.5±2.5 months (mean±SD). 7 patients (5.83%) withdrew; arm-level attribution not reported.

summary: This retrospective cohort study from a single clinic in South Korea evaluated a multi-drug 'Cocktail' treatment (Covi Wonder, comprising up to 17 medications including ivermectin, hydroxychloroquine, azithromycin, and others) versus no treatment in 47 long COVID patients who completed serial blood tests. The primary outcome was a proprietary 'blood toxicity score' based on stereomicroscopic identification of purported graphene oxide, microchips, and microrobots in blood samples. Treated patients (n=37) showed a statistically significant decrease in toxicity score (12.92±5.18 to 7.76±2.99, Wilcoxon z=-4.783, p<0.001), while untreated patients (n=10) showed a significant increase (12.90±7.20 to 18.30±5.25, p=0.011); however, the study is critically limited by its use of a pseudoscientific, unvalidated outcome measure, lack of randomization or blinding, very small sample size, and severe confounding.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC VALIDITY CONCERN: This paper's primary outcome measure — a 'blood toxicity score' based on stereomicroscopic identification of 'graphene oxide,' 'microchips,' 'microrobots,' and 'polyacrylamide hydrogel filaments' in blood — reflects pseudoscientific claims unsupported by mainstream biomedical evidence. The paper explicitly references COVID-19 vaccine conspiracy theories (including 'shedding,' VAIDS, self-assembling nanoparticles, and microchips) and is published in a low-impact open-access journal (Granthaalayah). The acknowledgment section honors a conspiracy figure jailed in Germany. Symptoms were assessed narratively without validated patient-reported outcome instruments — no quantitative symptom scores were extracted. The treatment duration of ~5 months 10 days was used to calculate treatment_duration_weeks (~22 weeks). Per-arm Ns for vaccinated/unvaccinated subgroups were inferred (treated arm: 27 vaccinated + 10 unvaccinated = 37; untreated arm: vaccination status not reported, so subgroup Ns for untreated arm are unknown). The Wilcoxon test p-values for the primary outcome are reported as z=-4.783, p<0.001 (treated) and z=-2.536, p=0.011 (untreated). This paper should not be included in a meta-analysis of evidence-based long COVID treatments.

summary: This retrospective single-center chart review evaluated 10 weekly sessions of red LED photobiomodulation (630 nm, 37 J/cm2) as adjuvant therapy for post-COVID telogen effluvium (TE) with or without androgenetic alopecia (AGA) in 140 long COVID patients divided into four groups. At 12 weeks, cessation of hair loss (negative hair pull test) occurred significantly more often in LED-treated TE patients (86.8% vs 48.1%, p<0.001) and TE+AGA patients (78.7% vs 46.2%, p=0.035) compared to controls without LED therapy. LED-treated groups also showed significant within-group increases in thick hair proportion and follicular unit density across frontal and occipital areas, while controls showed no significant improvement or worsening, supporting LED photobiomodulation as a promising adjuvant for post-COVID hair loss.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. summary: This multicenter prospective single-arm observational study (LIRA-COVID, n=83) evaluated oral L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA) 9 g/day for 4 weeks in Russian post-COVID syndrome patients with hyperammonemia, elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST >2x ULN), cognitive symptoms, and asthenia. After 4 weeks, blood ammonia decreased from 105.37±36.67 to 58.20±24.74 µmol/L (p<0.001), Number Connection Test time improved from 64.67±24.95 to 49.43±15.85 seconds (p<0.001), Asthenic Syndrome Scale score improved from 64.71±19.18 to 46.27±10.00 (p<0.001), and ALT and AST also significantly declined (all p<0.001). No adverse events were recorded, but the absence of a control group precludes causal inference.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Single-arm before-after study with no control group; all within-group p-values reported as p<0.001 (threshold, not exact). The paper is primarily in Russian with an English abstract; full quantitative data were extractable from both languages. Some demographic detail (comorbidity specifics) and Table 2 full contents were partially encoded in garbled Unicode (Cyrillic rendering issues in source text) but key numeric data were recoverable. Intermediate ammonia timepoint at Day 14 (78.90±30.43 µmol/L) extracted and included. HE stage distribution reported as percentages only, not raw counts (approximate n: no HE baseline ~5 patients, Stage 1 ~42, Stage 1-2 ~25, Stage 2 ~9, Stage 3 ~2; post-treatment: no HE ~34, Stage 1 ~30, Stage 1-2 ~19, Stage 2/3 ~0). Asthenia severity distribution pre/post also reported categorically (percentages only).

summary: This single-center prospective observational study compared 32 patients with biopsy-proven post-COVID myocarditis (SARS-CoV-2 RNA/protein positive) to 45 patients with non-COVID myocarditis, all treated with methylprednisolone-based immunosuppressive therapy. Post-COVID myocarditis was associated with significantly higher myocardial CD45 and CD68 cell counts and a broader morphological spectrum (including eosinophilic and giant cell variants). At follow-up, post-COVID patients had a significantly higher rate of excellent echocardiographic response (86% vs. 53% achieving ≥10% EF increase, p<0.05) and higher mean LV EF (49.8±7.6% vs. 43.9±12.3%, p<0.05), despite shorter follow-up and less frequent cytostatic use, though this comparison is substantially confounded by era-related differences in heart failure therapy.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. The overall follow-up was reported as median 15.0 [6.0; 35.5] months overall; per-arm medians were 9 [6;12] months (post-COVID) and 27 [15.5;35.5] months (non-COVID) — a major confounder. 2. Exact p-value for end-of-follow-up EF comparison stated only as p<0.05 in text. 3. TLR studies were performed in only 38 of 77 patients (subset not clearly allocated per arm in the paper). 4. Fig. 5 contains EF data at baseline and follow-up (extracted from text/tables) and an intermediate 'early treatment' timepoint (~4–6 months) — numeric values for the intermediate timepoint were not explicitly stated in text or tables, only visible in the figure; not extracted. 5. The multivariate regression for predictors of treatment response reported only that post-COVID myocarditis retained independent significance at p=0.20 (likely a typo for p<0.05 or reporting of the regression coefficient p-value rather than a threshold). 6. Additional IHC outcomes reported but not fully extracted: TLR4 endothelium (median non-COVID 5[2;6] vs. post-COVID 4[2;6], p=0.462), TLR4 macrophages (4[0;6] vs. 5[4;6], p=0.462), TLR9 endothelium (0[0;0] vs. 0[0;0], p=0.729), TLR9 macrophages (0[0;2] vs. 2[0;2], p=0.462), CD20 (0[0;0] both groups, p=0.345) — all non-significant.

summary: This is a post-hoc analysis of the single-arm LIRA-COVID observational program in which 83 Russian patients with post-COVID syndrome and hyperammonemia received oral L-ornithine L-aspartate (LOLA) 9 g/day for 4 weeks. All patients showed statistically significant pre-to-post improvements in ammonia, ALT, AST, Number Connection Test time, and asthenic state scores (all p<0.001). Post-hoc subgroup comparison of the 23 patients with co-existing NAFLD versus 60 without showed that NAFLD was associated with significantly higher baseline AST (p=0.043) and slower ammonia reduction at day 14 (p=0.033), suggesting NAFLD patients may require longer treatment courses.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Paper is a post-hoc analysis of the previously published LIRA-COVID study; there is no randomization or control group — all 83 patients received LOLA. The three 'arms' represent the overall sample and two post-hoc subgroups (NAFLD vs. no-NAFLD), not parallel treatment groups. Table 1 reports overall sample (n=83); Table 3 reports NAFLD subgroup (n=23); Table 4 reports no-NAFLD subgroup (n=60). Ammonia is measured at 3 timepoints (day 0, 14, 28), other outcomes only at day 0 and 28. The paper does not report exact arm-level p-values for the within-group changes in NAFLD and no-NAFLD subgroups — p-value thresholds used (p<0.01 for NAFLD, p<0.001 for no-NAFLD). The p-values for between-group differences (NAFLD vs. no-NAFLD for AST baseline and ammonia day 14) are stated verbatim (p=0.043 and p=0.033 respectively). Adverse events were registered but no quantitative data were reported. The overall sample NCT/AST/ALT/ShAS values in Table 1 differ slightly from the weighted sum of NAFLD and no-NAFLD subgroup values — this may reflect rounding or different statistical representations.

summary: This prospective cohort study from Ukraine followed 266 hospitalized moderate-to-severe COVID-19 patients for one year; 25 (9.4%) were diagnosed with post-COVID-19 interstitial lung disease (ILD), of whom 9 received off-label nintedanib 300 mg/day for 3 months in addition to corticosteroids. Nintedanib did not significantly affect radiological pulmonary fibrosis pattern (p=1.000), ILD progression (p=0.180), post-6MWT oxygen saturation (p=0.411), or dyspnea index (p=0.451) compared to corticosteroid-only treatment. The authors conclude that antifibrotic therapy for post-COVID-19 ILD should be individualized and used for longer than 3 months only in those with clinically significant pulmonary fibrosis patterns, pending further evidence from controlled trials.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Paper is primarily in Ukrainian with English abstract and partial English results. No per-arm means or SDs were reported for any outcome — only p-values from non-parametric tests (Mann-Whitney U, median test) comparing nintedanib vs. no-nintedanib groups. Arm 2 n=16 is calculated (25 total minus 9 nintedanib). The overall cohort was 58.8% female but per-arm sex breakdown not reported. FVC and FEV1 are mentioned in context of disease progression correlation but no per-arm numeric values provided. The study is observational with physician-decided (not randomized) treatment assignment. Two p-values given for the SpO2 outcome (p=0.411 median test; p=0.329 Mann-Whitney U) and two for dyspnea (p=0.451 and p=0.422) — the median test p-values were used as primary. 1.9% mortality reported in the overall cohort of 266 over the follow-up year.

summary: This prospective observational study from Ukraine examined 45 post-COVID patients (mean age 61 years) who had experienced community-acquired pneumonia due to COVID-19, comparing those who received extended post-acute anticoagulation (rivaroxaban or apixaban for median 63 days; n=25) versus those who did not (n=20). No thrombotic events occurred in the anticoagulation group, while 5/20 (25%) patients in the non-anticoagulation group developed thrombosis (predominantly pulmonary embolism) at a median of 40 days from COVID onset (16 days after stopping acute-phase anticoagulants). Severe acute COVID-19 was a significant risk factor for post-COVID thrombosis in the absence of anticoagulation (p=0.04), while hereditary thrombophilia was an additional risk factor; however, the groups were not comparable at baseline due to confounding by indication.

summary: This retrospective EHR cohort study (n=1,207) examined whether systemic inflammation during COVID-19 hospitalization — measured by peak CRP — was associated with all-cause mortality in the 12 months following hospital discharge, and whether oral steroid prescriptions at discharge modified this risk. Elevated CRP (top vs. bottom 50%) was independently associated with increased post-discharge mortality (adjusted HR 1.61, 95% CI 1.19–2.20), and this finding was consistent using tertile splits. Oral steroid prescriptions at discharge were associated with significantly reduced post-discharge mortality (adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.33–0.74), suggesting anti-inflammatory treatment after acute COVID-19 may reduce downstream mortality risk, though the observational design limits causal inference.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This study is primarily about post-acute COVID-19 mortality risk associated with inflammation (CRP), not a long COVID treatment trial per se. The 'treatment' comparison is oral steroid prescription at hospital discharge vs. none — a physician-decided, observational exposure subject to confounding by indication. Arms 3–5 in outcome 2–3 represent CRP tertile groupings (not steroid arms); arms 6–10 in outcome 4 represent severity subgroups (no O2, supplemental O2, ventilator) and dexamethasone vs. no dexamethasone groups for CRP means. Per-arm mortality event counts for the steroid vs. no-steroid comparison are not reported in the paper — only the overall cohort total (n=175, 14.5%) and tertile-specific totals are given in Table 1. The Kaplan-Meier figure shows survival curves but numeric values are only available from the figure (not extracted). The CRP SD for patients not on dexamethasone appears as '90/8' in the paper, interpreted as 90.8 mg/L (likely OCR/formatting error for ±).

summary: This multicentric prospective cohort study in Ecuador enrolled 477 adults who received 8 weeks of multidisciplinary rehabilitation (3x/week) at 14 centers, comparing functional and perceived health outcomes between 354 patients with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and 123 without PCC over 12 weeks. Overall, PCFS functional status improved significantly (mean decrease 0.48 points, 95% CI -0.65 to -0.31, p<0.0001) and perceived health (AVS) improved by 0.68 points (95% CI 0.56-0.80, p<0.0001); however, PCC patients had substantially lower odds of achieving a favorable PCFS outcome at Week 12 compared to non-PCC patients (aOR 0.27, 95% CI 0.13-0.56, p<0.001), while AVS improvement did not differ significantly by PCC status (aOR 0.58, p=0.062). The study lacked a no-treatment control group, and nearly half of participants did not complete the 12-week assessment.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a single-arm intervention study (all participants received the same rehabilitation) stratified by exposure status (PCC vs non-PCC) rather than a true two-arm trial. Per-arm mean PCFS and AVS scores at each timepoint are NOT reported numerically in text or tables — only overall change-from-baseline statistics and logistic regression ORs for achieving favorable outcomes are reported. Baseline PCFS distribution is given categorically (grades 0-4 counts by group) but not as means/SDs. AVS baseline distribution is also only categorical. Symptom trajectory data (Figure 1) is available only for the PCC subgroup (not non-PCC). arm_id=0 used in within_group_change entries to indicate overall cohort (both arms combined), as the paper reports these as overall mixed-effects model results without arm stratification. Outcome 2 was added to capture intermediate timepoint changes for the overall cohort PCFS. No adverse events were reported.

summary: This single-arm retrospective medical records review (n=40) evaluated 10 sessions of major ozone autohemotherapy (MBO) in post-COVID syndrome patients at a Turkish university hospital, measuring fatigue (FACIT), anxiety and depression (Beck scales), sleep quality (PSQI), and quality of life (SF-36) before and after treatment. Statistically significant pre-to-post improvements were observed across nearly all outcomes: FACIT fatigue (median 31 to 9.5, p=0.001), Beck anxiety (7.5 to 4.0, p=0.001), Beck depression (5.5 to 1.0, p=0.002), global PSQI (15 to 13, p=0.016), and 8 of 9 SF-36 subscales (all p<0.05), with emotional well-being the only non-significant subscale. The study lacks a control group, so causal attribution to MBO is not possible.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Single-arm before-after study only; no control group. All data reported as median (min-max) using Wilcoxon signed-rank test — no means or SDs available. The min-max range is reported in tables, not IQR; iqr_low and iqr_high fields have been populated with the min and max values respectively as the only range data available. Treatment session duration in weeks not explicitly stated (10 sessions at 2-3x/week implies approximately 3.3–5 weeks but not confirmed). No adverse events reported. Vaccine status: 85% vaccinated (n=34 of 40). The PSQI sleep duration subscore median is identical pre and post (both 7) yet p=0.008, consistent with a non-parametric rank-based test on the full distribution. Post-treatment follow-up appears to be at end of treatment only (no subsequent follow-up visits described).

summary: This single-center, uncontrolled, prospective observational cohort study enrolled 72 patients (mean age 54.6 years, 67% female) hospitalized with post-COVID-19 intestinal lesions (GI symptoms arising 2-4 weeks after COVID-19 recovery with negative PCR) during the first and second COVID-19 waves in Russia (June 2020-September 2021). All patients had diarrhea (mean 6.8 episodes/day), with highly variable endoscopic findings including pseudomembranous colitis (17.9%), focal hemorrhagic colitis (16.4%), erosions (28.4%), newly diagnosed ulcerative colitis (3%), and normal or near-normal mucosa (31.3%); C. difficile toxins were detected in 38.9%. Treatment was symptomatic; 56.9% improved during hospitalization, 27.8% achieved complete recovery within 4-8 weeks, while 3 patients (4.2%) required emergency colectomy and 2 (2.8%) died, with no consistent correlation between clinical severity and endoscopic/histologic findings.

summary: This single-arm longitudinal observational study followed 127 post-COVID patients (76% female, mean age 51 years, 70% healthcare workers) through a mean 29-day inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation program in Germany, with assessments at rehabilitation start (T1) and 6 (T3) and 12 months (T4) post-discharge. summary: This multicentre prospective observational cohort study followed 88 post-COVID-19 patients (mean age 54.4 years, 48.9% male) from five Dutch hospitals, measuring symptoms monthly from 4 to 18 months post-infection. Using latent class mixed modelling, three distinct trajectories were identified for both fatigue and dyspnoea: decreasing, high persistent, and low persistent. Participation in a lifestyle intervention (personalised dietary and physical activity counselling) was significantly associated with higher odds of symptom improvement (decreasing fatigue OR 1.58; decreasing dyspnoea OR 2.21), while female sex, older age, comorbidities, and mild acute COVID-19 severity were associated with persistent high-burden trajectories.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is primarily a trajectory analysis study, not a treatment RCT. The 'lifestyle intervention' was offered to participants as an optional component of the cohort study (self-selected, not randomised; n=42 participated). All between-group effect estimates are multinomial logistic regression ORs comparing trajectories vs 'high persistent' reference category. No numeric outcome data per trajectory subgroup is available (data only in figures). Detailed monthly frequency data per symptom are in Figure S1 (supplementary, not extractable from this text).

summary: This single-arm longitudinal pilot study assessed the Adaptive Force (AF), a measure of neuromuscular holding capacity, in 17 long COVID patients at three time points: during long COVID state (pre), immediately after first individualized integrative medicine treatment (post), and at recovery (end, ~71 days later). The maximal isometric Adaptive Force (AFisomax) was severely reduced at baseline (elbow: 87.9 N, hip: 88.3 N, ~47-49% of maximal AF) and increased significantly to near-normal levels post-treatment and at recovery (elbow: 187.2 N, hip: 174.1 N, ~100% of maximal AF; all p<0.0001, Cohen's d >2.4). Symptom intensities across 13 domains (fatigue 7.75, post-exertion malaise 8.14, and others) also decreased significantly from long COVID state to recovery, though the uncontrolled design, self-selected recovery endpoint, and heterogeneous individualized treatments preclude causal attribution.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1) This is a single-arm before-after study with no control group; the 'end' timepoint was defined as recovery/substantial health improvement, creating major ascertainment bias (only recovered patients were included). 2) The 20 patients who had not recovered by July 2022 were excluded, so the sample is highly selected. 3) Demographic data reported separately by sex (14 female, 3 male) with separate age/height/weight statistics; combined mean age not explicitly reported. 4) The weeks_from_enrollment for 'end' was calculated as 71.06 days ÷ 7 ≈ 10.15 weeks. 5) Some AFmax hip flexor CI values in Table 2 appear to have a typographical error (pre CI lower bound listed as 148.77;148.77 — likely should be 148.77;201.20); extracted as printed. 6) Symptom data n=14 at pre and n=13 at end (one patient did not complete follow-up questionnaire). 7) Additional symptoms reported in Table 3 (fever) were omitted from outcomes extraction but noted: fever pre=2.14±3.66, end=0.23±0.83, p=0.023. 8) Ratio of AFosc to AFisomax (%) and Ratio of AFosc to AFmax (%) outcomes were partially extracted via narrative but full per-timepoint tabular data are available in Table 2 for completeness — these were not separately entered as outcome objects to keep JSON manageable. 9) The integrative medicine treatment involved PEMF, mental stress treatment, and lymphatic/osteopathic techniques; it was individualized and non-standardized.

summary: This 12-week prospective observational study in Romania enrolled 505 post-COVID-19 patients with fatigue, assigning 146 to Astenor Energy (arginine aspartate + B6 + biotin + magnesium) and 359 to Astenor Forte (L-arginine + malic acid) based on physician-assessed liver enzyme levels. Both groups showed statistically significant reductions in FAS fatigue scores after 3 months of treatment (Group 1: median 33 to 17; Group 2: median 25 to 17; both p<0.0001), with 68.7% of all patients reaching no-fatigue status at follow-up compared to 27.7% at baseline. However, the non-randomized allocation and large baseline differences in COVID-19 severity between groups preclude conclusions about the relative efficacy of the two formulations or causal attribution of improvement to the supplements.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a two-arm non-randomized prospective observational study, not an RCT. Groups differed substantially at baseline in COVID-19 severity (48.7% vs 82.5% mild/asymptomatic) because allocation was by physician decision based on ALT/AST levels. No between-group comparison for FAS change from baseline was reported or is appropriate given confounding. The overall FAS mean ± SD of 27.69 ± 9.34 applies to the full cohort of 505 at baseline; sex-stratified FAS means are also reported for the full cohort. Physical and mental subscale means (14.77±4.51 and 12.91±5.26) are for the full cohort at baseline. IQR values for FAS by arm at baseline and follow-up are not reported numerically in the text (only medians given). ALT and AST changes were noted as significant in figures (p<0.0001 noted in figure legend) but exact p-values for within-group change not stated in text for each arm separately. Funding by BIESSEN Pharma (manufacturer of the supplements studied) is a significant conflict of interest. No ITT/CONSORT flow reported; no dropouts mentioned.

summary: This prospective observational study compared inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) outcomes among 483 post-acute COVID-19 patients from four pandemic waves (Feb 2020–Jun 2022) at a single Swiss rehabilitation center, grouped into Wave 1+2 (n=253, older, more comorbid) vs Wave 3+4 (n=230, younger, more functionally impaired). Wave 3+4 patients showed significantly greater improvements in both 6-MWT (188m vs 147m gain, p<0.001) and FIM (21.1 vs 15.6 points gain, p<0.001), likely attributable to their younger age and greater baseline functional impairment rather than the rehabilitation program itself.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Exact post-intervention (22-month) symptom prevalence percentages are only shown in Figure 4 (bar chart) and not provided as numeric values in the text or any table — thus timepoint_id=2 percent values for outcomes 1-8 are set to null with result_source='not_reported'. Baseline symptom frequencies at 15 months are described in approximate terms ('more than 90%', 'more than 75%', 'more than half', 'around 40%') rather than exact counts — these were recorded as approximate percent values with result_source='inferred'. Patient-perceived improvement breakdown: 9% healthy/complete recovery, 33% moderate improvement, 20% minimal improvement, 38% no improvement. Return-to-work breakdown (n=40 excluding 5 retired): 36% no work, 24% partial (>=50%), 40% full-time. No validated questionnaires were used; all symptom data are non-standardized self-report. summary: This prospective before-after cohort study assessed 34 post-acute COVID-19 patients undergoing a 28-day inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation program (exercise, nutritional therapy, psychiatric support) in Italy, comparing outcomes in those with sarcopenia (n=20) versus without (n=14) at admission. summary: This single-arm observational study of 10 post-COVID ME/CFS patients with elevated ADRB2 autoantibodies assessed the effect of immunoadsorption (5 sessions over 10 days) on physical function. summary: This single-center Romanian cohort study assessed long-term disability ~3 years after post-acute rehabilitation in 27 survivors of severe/critical COVID-19 using the WHODAS 2.0 questionnaire administered by telephone. The rehabilitation intervention was an inpatient multidisciplinary program (median 18 days) based on the STM ASAP protocol, applied immediately post-discharge from acute COVID-19 care. The overall disability score at 3-year follow-up was 35.09%, with highest impairment in household activities (51.79%) and participation in society (39.81%); central neurological deficits were significantly associated with higher disability across all six domains (r=0.495–0.683, p<0.01), while ICU admission was paradoxically negatively correlated with disability scores in most domains, possibly reflecting a rehabilitation benefit.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a single-arm observational cohort study with no control group and no baseline WHODAS 2.0 measurement — disability was assessed only once at ~3-year follow-up, so no pre-post within-group change can be extracted. The 'work/school activities' subscore was completed by only 6 of 27 patients (those still working). The rehabilitation hospitalization duration is reported as both 'median 18 (11.5, 24) days' (IQR) in one table and 'average 19.14 ± 8.06 days' (mean ± SD) elsewhere — both are noted. The study reports Spearman/Pearson correlation coefficients between WHODAS domain scores and clinical variables (DM, ICU admission, central neurological deficit), extracted in subgroup analyses. No formal between-group comparisons with effect sizes (mean differences, ORs) are reported. The overall disability score is stated as 35.09% in the Results table but as 35.9% in the Discussion — 35.09% used as primary value.

summary: This prospective single-arm longitudinal observational study enrolled 127 post-COVID patients (predominantly healthcare workers with work-related COVID-19) who completed a mean 29-day multidisciplinary inpatient rehabilitation program in Germany, with follow-up at 6 months (T3, n=108-121) and 12 months (T4, n=95-115) post-rehabilitation. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Single-arm before-after study with no control group; all comparisons are within-group (Wilcoxon signed-rank, T1 vs T3 and T1 vs T4). The study reports median (IQR) for all continuous outcomes due to non-normal distributions. Effect sizes reported as Wilcoxon r (not Cohen's d). The T1 sample size for spiroergometry outcomes (VO2max, Wattmax) differs slightly between T3 (n=50) and T4 (n=51) analyses, likely due to different paired samples. Time since infection mean 409.52 days (SD=143.97) = ~13.65 months (SD ~4.8 months). Treatment duration calculated as ~4 weeks (mean 28.99 days). Total follow-up from T1 to T4 approximately 56 weeks (29 days rehab + ~12 months follow-up). PCFS p-value at T3 stated as 0.790 in text but r=-0.219 in table (r value may be from Friedman or different analysis; extracted as stated). Baseline T1 n for 6MWT and quadricep at T3 is 108 vs 107 for 1MSTST at T3; minor discrepancy likely due to missing values. summary: This retrospective before-after study evaluated the effectiveness of inpatient health resort treatment (mean ~24.6 days) for cardiopulmonary symptoms of long COVID in 122 patients (mean age 64.4 years) at a Polish sanatorium in 2021. The complex multimodal intervention included balneotherapy, respiratory and general exercises, physical medicine modalities (LLLT, cryotherapy, TENS, electromagnetic fields), and health education. All assessed cardiopulmonary symptom domains improved significantly after treatment (p<0.05 for 7 of 8 outcomes), including mMRC dyspnoea (62% decrease, from 1.37 to 0.52 points, p<0.0001), exercise-induced dyspnoea (63% decrease), sputum (82% decrease), and cough intensity (81% decrease), with fast heart rate being the only non-significant outcome (p=0.06). summary: This prospective observational study compared outcomes of a 2-6 week supervised inpatient post-COVID-19 rehabilitation program (breathing exercises, aerobic training, and strength training) in 84 patients with metabolic syndrome (MetS) versus 62 without MetS at a single rehabilitation hospital in Poland. subgroup_analyses.results_summary: Normal BMI patients had highest admission mean (437.62m) and discharge mean (505.77m); overweight had admission 398m, discharge 476.12m; obese had admission 358m, discharge 420m. Normal BMI patients also had lowest Borg scores throughout.

Patients without lung damage walked further at admission (466m) and discharge (536.18m) compared to those with lung damage (370.29m and 440.58m respectively); lung damage correlated negatively with 6MWT at both timepoints (p<0.05).

Patients without musculoskeletal damage had lower admission 6MWT (386.82m) but also lower discharge 6MWT (458.73m) compared to those with musculoskeletal damage (admission 424.57m, discharge 498.24m), likely confounded by HILT treatment in the musculoskeletal group.

Patients with cardiac damage had substantially lower admission 6MWT (336.29m) and discharge 6MWT (426.43m) vs. those without (429.15m and 494.50m); cardiac damage correlated with higher Borg exertion at discharge (p<0.05, r=0.382).

Patients with neurological damage had higher admission 6MWT (426.80m) and discharge 6MWT (488.13m) vs. those without (383.42m and 457.83m), possibly reflecting confounding with the HILT group composition.

summary: This retrospective before-after study compared 10-day rehabilitation programs in 33 post-COVID patients: HILT plus kinesiotherapy (n=18, all with musculoskeletal disorders) versus kinesiotherapy alone (n=15, without musculoskeletal disorders). Both groups improved on the 6-Minute Walk Test, with the HILT group achieving a higher mean discharge distance (519m vs. 445.73m) and a statistically significant association between HILT and greater distance yield (p<0.01, r=-0.666 in the correlation analysis). However, the two groups differed fundamentally in their comorbidity profiles, making attribution of benefit specifically to HILT versus differences in underlying pathology unreliable.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Several issues: (1) Tables had significant rendering artifacts with merged/duplicated cells requiring careful parsing. (2) The correlation between HILT and discharge distance was reported as r=-0.692 (negative), which appears counterintuitive — likely a coding artifact where HILT=0 and no-HILT=1, so the negative r actually indicates HILT associated with higher distance. (3) No SDs were reported for any outcome means — only min/max ranges provided. (4) The 6MWT yield (distance yield, %) was referenced in correlation analyses and figures but arm-specific means were not tabulated in numeric form. (5) Overall cohort O2 saturation ranges given but not broken down by arm. (6) One patient (of 33) could not complete 6MWT (96.96% completion = 32/33); unclear which arm this patient belonged to. (7) No p-values reported for within-group pre-post changes; only between-group correlations with HILT variable reported. (8) The between-group effect for 6MWT yield is from the correlation analysis (r=-0.666, p<0.01) not a formal group comparison.

summary: This prospective observational cohort study examined 94 post-ICU COVID-19 patients in Spain, grouped by serum vitamin D levels (deficient ≤20, insufficient 20-30, sufficient ≥30 ng/mL) at 14-21 days post-discharge, and followed through a 6-month multispecialty rehabilitation program including vitamin D supplementation for deficient/insufficient patients. summary: This retrospective population-based observational study from the Consorci Sanitari de Terrassa (n=192,651), Spain, compared long COVID incidence and thrombotic events in patients chronically prescribed antihistamines versus those not on antihistamines over five years (March 2020–March 2025). Thrombotic events were significantly less frequent in antihistamine users across multiple polypharmacy strata and calendar years (overall 1.6% vs 3.3%, p<0.0001), with ORs ranging from 1.5 to 9.0 in individual annual/polypharmacy subgroup comparisons, and logistic regression confirmed an independent inverse association between antihistamine use and thrombosis after adjusting for age, sex, and number of chronic treatments.

summary: This retrospective before-after study at a single TMS clinic in Tokyo examined the effect of 10 sessions of rTMS on psychiatric and physical symptoms in 60 patients with long COVID (n=46) or post-COVID-19-vaccination symptoms (n=14). All four symptom measures (QIDS, PHQ9, GAD7, Performance Status) improved significantly after TMS in both groups. The primary finding was that higher baseline fatigue severity (Performance Status score) was independently associated with worse improvement in depression (QIDS) after TMS, across multiple adjusted MANCOVA models (partial regression coefficient ~0.50–0.53, p=0.03–0.04), suggesting fatigue may impede TMS-induced depression recovery in this population.

summary: This quasi-experimental study from Odessa, Ukraine enrolled 42 couples (84 individuals) who had COVID-19 within the prior year; 21 couples received personalized preconception preparation (including nutritional supplementation with Methylfolate-containing complexes, vitamin D, magnesium, antiplatelet agents, and infectious focus treatment, starting 3-4 months before planned conception at least 6 months post-COVID), while 21 couples conceived spontaneously 1-3 months post-COVID without preparation. Across all three trimesters, the intervention group had significantly lower rates of threatened miscarriage (9.5% vs 33.3%), early toxicosis (14.3% vs 38.1%), anemia in the first trimester (0% vs 52.4%), and anemia in the third trimester (0% vs 44.4%), with statistically significant differences (p<0.05). The study is severely limited by non-random self-selected group assignment and uncontrolled confounding, making causal inference unreliable.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Paper is written in Ukrainian with an English abstract. This is a preconception/obstetric intervention study for post-COVID women planning pregnancy — it is not strictly a long COVID treatment trial but addresses reproductive outcomes in post-COVID patients. Table 1 (baseline labs) reports only single mean values with no SDs for women (group Iж, n=21) and men (group Iч, n=21) in the intervention arm only — no baseline lab data for the comparison group. Comparison group (IIж) reduced from n=21 to n=18 in 2nd and 3rd trimesters due to pregnancy losses in 1st trimester (3 cases: spontaneous abortion n=1, failed abortion n=1, anembryonia n=1). Table 3 has complex merged cells and some inconsistencies in reported denominators between trimesters. Some second trimester complication rows (e.g., placental abruption row) appear to have missing/ambiguous data for arm 1 due to table formatting issues. Antifetal death (5.6%, n=1 in group IIж, 2nd trimester) and congenital malformations (second trimester, 5.6% in IIж) were not extracted as separate outcomes but are noted. Third trimester: placental dysfunction (14.3% Iж vs 16.7% IIж, marked as significant), placental abruption (0% vs 11.1% IIж) also present in Table 3 but omitted from outcome list for brevity. The age reported for men is 25±2 years (verbatim); women 24±2 years — these appear to apply to the overall sample since groups were stated to be representative/comparable. No SD reported for any laboratory measure. No post-intervention laboratory follow-up values reported for the comparison group.

summary: This retrospective single-arm observational study evaluated a personalized exercise reconditioning program (6 days/week, 150 min/day of aerobic training including cycle ergometer, treadmill, and calisthenics) in 24 patients with post-COVID pathology syndrome and chronic respiratory insufficiency admitted for inpatient rehabilitation in Italy (mean stay 53 days). Significant improvements were observed in 6-minute walk test distance (median 0m to 330m, p<0.001), FIM functional independence score (87 to 120, p<0.001), mMRC dyspnea (4 to 2, p<0.001), FiO2 (25% to 21%, p<0.001), and Borg fatigue and dyspnea scores (both 10 to 3, p<0.001), while blood gas parameters (PaO2, PaCO2) did not change significantly. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. Single-arm pre-post study; no control group. summary: This retrospective single-arm before-after study evaluated a 3-week pulmonary rehabilitation programme conducted in the underground salt chambers of the Wieliczka Salt Mine Health Resort in 591 post-COVID patients (mean age 60, 59% female, mean 7.4 months post-infection). summary: This retrospective cohort study from a single Korean hospital examined 91 patients with post-COVID-19 organizing pneumonia who required hospitalization for corticosteroid treatment, comparing those treated earlier (<18.4 days from COVID-19 diagnosis, n=55) versus later (≥18.4 days, n=36). extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Groups were defined by physician-decided timing of steroid initiation rather than randomization; this is a retrospective observational study with meaningful baseline differences (CT findings, SpO2/FiO2). Total follow-up duration was calculated from mean total steroid duration (49.4 days ÷ 7 = 7.1 weeks). SD values for the outpatient steroid requirement are reported as '0.1±0.0' and '0.1±0.1' — these appear to be rounded. Paper explicitly notes adverse events were not compared between groups. summary: This prospective cohort study conducted across four Russian medical centers compared a multidisciplinary rehabilitation program (aquatic exercises, respiratory/motor exercises, neuropsychologic sessions, LASER therapy, and magnetotherapy; n=25) against three comparators — eastern medicine techniques (n=25), balneotherapy/physiotherapy (n=29), and home-based self-training (n=34) — in long COVID patients followed for 6 months post-rehabilitation via structured telephone interview. The experimental group had substantially fewer hospital admissions (4% vs 28%, 6.9%, and 11.8%) and far fewer GP consultations (16% vs 68%, 65.5%, and 58.8%), with RR reductions of 85.7%, 42%, and 66% for hospitalizations compared to the three groups respectively; the hospitalization difference was statistically significant versus CG1 (p=0.021) but not CG2 or CG3. However, the groups were recruited at different sites with significant baseline differences in comorbidities (notably obesity 48% EG vs 0% in CG1 and CG3), making causal interpretation difficult.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. The study is described as 'randomized, parallel-group' in the methods but the groups were recruited at entirely different medical centers — this is more accurately a multi-site comparative cohort study with non-random assignment. 2. The RR values are reported with a non-standard format (e.g., '0.143±1.031') where the ±value appears to be the SE of the log RR or a related statistic, not a conventional ± SD; these have been extracted in the SE field of the between_group_effects for the hospital admissions outcome. 3. The chi-square statistics for the 'need for therapeutic care' outcome (χ²=6.635, p=0.001; χ²=13.463, p=0.001; χ²=10.949, p=0.001) appear to refer to the composite 'request for care' outcome and are mapped to the GP consultations outcome as the most numerically complete proxy. 4. No continuous/quantitative symptom outcomes (e.g., fatigue scores, 6MWT, QoL instruments) are reported — all outcomes are binary event counts from the telephone follow-up. 5. Percent female per arm was calculated from the text stating 7 male patients in EG (28% male = 72% female), 5 in CG1 (20% male = 80% female), 8 in CG2 (27.6% male = 72.4% female), 10 in CG3 (29.4% male = 70.6% female). 6. The dropout of 7 patients (5.83%) is noted but not allocated per arm. 7. Table 1 has a formatting artifact where the 'Less than 50% CT lung damage' row for EG appears merged — 18 (72%) extracted for EG from that row.

summary: This single-center before-after study examined how TLR4 Asp299Gly genetic polymorphism modifies rehabilitation outcomes in 92 post-COVID syndrome patients with respiratory manifestations who received inpatient multimodal rehabilitation (climatotherapy, exercise therapy, massage, aromatherapy, respiratory therapy) in Yalta, Russia. Patients were stratified by genotype into AA (n=22), AG (n=37), and GG (n=33) groups, with no randomization or control arm. All genotype groups showed within-group improvements in fatigue, dyspnea, SpO2, and quality of life, but AG heterozygotes demonstrated the largest and most statistically significant improvements across clinical symptoms, pulmonary function, 6MWT distance (+49m vs +13m in GG), and anxiety scores, while AA homozygotes showed the least functional improvement; however, between-group differences did not reach statistical significance for most outcomes.

summary: This retrospective comparative review examined the impact of COVID-19 pandemic-related restructuring on inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation across a network of 8 Italian hospitals, comparing 2,089 patients admitted during March 2020–March 2021 (including 265 with post-COVID sequelae, 12.7%) to 3,912 patients admitted in the preceding year. Despite a 47% reduction in admissions and significant case-mix changes, rehabilitation outcomes (6MWT, MRC dyspnoea, CAT, SPPB, Barthel dyspnoea) were broadly similar between periods, though COVID-era patients had worse baseline disability (Barthel 60 vs 69) and achieved greater functional gains. In-hospital mortality (2.2% vs 1.6%) and acute hospital transfers (8.0% vs 3.3%) were higher in the COVID era, while home discharge rates were lower (88.5% vs 93.6%); no statistical tests or p-values were reported for any between-group comparisons.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is primarily a health service reconfiguration review, not a long COVID treatment trial. The 265 post-COVID sequelae patients represent only 12.7% of the COVID-era cohort; all outcome data are reported for the entire mixed-diagnosis cohort (CRF, COPD, OSAS, ILD, tracheostomized, post-COVID), not specifically for the post-COVID subgroup. No statistical tests or p-values are reported for any between-group or within-group comparisons. LOS means are reported (23.84±16.14 vs 23.37±12.37 days) but not extracted as a formal outcome. Nursing home discharge rates also reported (1.24% COVID vs 1.47% pre-COVID). Individual patient follow-up duration is not reported; LOS approximates treatment duration but exact rehabilitation duration per patient is not given.

summary: This retrospective multicenter observational study examined whether COVID-19 vaccination status influenced outcomes of an inpatient pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) program in 96 severe COVID-19 survivors (46 vaccinated, 50 unvaccinated) admitted to three ICS Maugeri IRCCS hospitals in Italy between September 2021 and April 2022. CT/CXR findings extracted from Tables 2 and 3 but not repeated as separate outcome objects for every sub-finding (e.g. diffuse reticulations, GGOs) to manage output size; key radiological summary outcomes (normal CXR, normal HRCT) are included. Arterial blood gas values (pH 7.43±0.024, pCO2 36.14±2.53, paO2 51.28±2.54) reported for the 7 hypoxic patients only at baseline — no follow-up ABG data available for extraction. summary: This descriptive retrospective study used Romania's National DRG administrative database to characterize 567 confirmed COVID-19 patients who received their first episode of inpatient medical rehabilitation between April 2020 and September 2021. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Study design is observational (non-randomized), with arm assignment by baseline VO2max rather than randomization — arms differ significantly by age (p=0.030) and sex (p=0.002). summary: This prospective single-center cohort study from rural Bihar, India, enrolled 27 children with WHO-defined MIS-C (median age 8 years) between June 2021 and April 2022; 85% were treated with pulse methylprednisolone and 15% with IVIG based on affordability. summary: This observational cohort study from Kazakhstan compared 49 post-COVID-19 patients who received two doses of Gam-COVID-Vac (Sputnik V) vaccine with 46 unvaccinated post-COVID-19 patients, all assessed approximately 12 months after vaccination or acute infection for neurological symptoms and immune parameters. summary: This single-arm before-after study evaluated a 3-month supervised Physical Rehabilitation Program (breathing exercises, strength training, aerobic exercise 2-3x/week) in 18 post-COVID-19 patients with long COVID sequelae in Brazil. The program produced large-to-huge improvements in handgrip strength (26.5 to 31.8 kgf, Cohen's d=2.7, p=0.001), maximal inspiratory pressure (80.6 to 108.3 cmH2O, d=1.6, p<0.001), maximal expiratory pressure (106.4 to 131.8 cmH2O, d=2.7, p=0.001), and estimated VO2peak (17.2 to 27.8 ml/kg/min, d=2.3, p<0.001) and 6-minute step test performance (93.3 to 140.6 steps, d=1.6, p<0.001). Despite these functional gains, heart rate recovery at 1 minute (a mortality risk marker) did not significantly improve (p=0.052), with 72% still showing abnormal recovery post-PRP.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Single-arm pre-post study; no control group. Delta (ΔPRP) values in Table 2 are reported as negative for improvements in HGS and respiratory pressures, which is likely a sign convention issue in the table header — the absolute difference (post minus pre) would be positive for HGS (+5.3), MIP (+27.7), MEP (+25.3); stored as reported. Table 3 delta for HR at rest is listed as 10.3 (positive = reduction from 88 to 77.7, table sign may reflect magnitude not direction). Cohen's d values provided in tables represent within-group effect sizes (not between-group). Correlation figures (Figures 2-3) referenced but no numeric correlation coefficients extractable from text. VO2 classification distribution (very weak/weak/regular/good/excellent) extracted as counts in Table 3. Sarcopenia row (1/1 pre/post) unchanged, p=NA — not extracted as separate outcome. Hospitalization data reported as median (8 days, range 5-30) for the subset hospitalized, but proportion hospitalized not clearly stated. No adverse events reported anywhere in the paper.

summary: This single-arm prospective observational study from Bangladesh examined the outcomes of pulmonary rehabilitation in 126 long COVID patients (83% male, age 18–52 years) attending a tertiary hospital between May and December 2023. All participants completed pulmonary rehabilitation (88.9% center-based), and pre-post comparisons showed mean FEV1 increased from 3.2 to 4.5 L in males and 2.3 to 3.1 L in females, and FVC from 3.5 to 5.5 L (males) and 2.5 to 3.7 L (females), with VAS pain scores also improving; 92.9% of participants showed improved CPET results. No control group, statistical tests, SDs, or p-values were reported, preventing any formal inference about efficacy.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Multiple serious data quality issues: (1) No SDs reported for any continuous outcome. (2) No p-values or statistical tests reported for within-group changes. (3) Rehabilitation program duration not specified — the referenced '20 days' is cited from a different study in the literature review, not from this study's own protocol. (4) 6MWT data only reported as a range (350–850 m) with no mean or SD, and it is unclear whether this is baseline, post-treatment, or both. (5) Fatigue data reported only as baseline categorical distribution, no post-treatment fatigue data extracted. (6) Study design described as 'prospective observational study' in the abstract but 'cross sectional study design' in the methodology — treated as before-after single-arm. (7) Abstract states '880.9%' center-based (obvious typo for 88.09% or 88.1%), and table section confirms 111/126 = 88.1% center-based. (8) ADL reported only at end of study with no baseline comparison available. (9) CPET 'improved more' vs 'improved less' is not a validated or standardized outcome measure. (10) This is published in a low-impact open-access journal (IRJMETS, impact factor self-reported as 7.868) with hallmarks of low methodological quality.

summary: This prospective, single-arm observational cohort study evaluated a 2-week spa-based respiratory rehabilitation program (inhalation therapy, respiratory physiotherapy, hydrokinesitherapy) in 187 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent dyspnoea at a health resort in southern Italy. After treatment, 88.2% reported dyspnoea improvement and 80.6% reported fatigue improvement; in the 118-patient subgroup assessed with validated scales, median Borg exertion dyspnoea score improved from 3.60 to 1.41 and median Barthel Index improved from 74.00 to 86.55, with approximately 51% of patients reaching MCID thresholds for each. Outcome 10 (Barthel by sex) uses subgroup data from Table 8 to capture the reported between-group p-value (p=0.006 for male vs female pre-treatment Barthel). summary: This retrospective observational study from a tertiary care hospital in India described the microbial profile and antibiotic resistance patterns of 84 long COVID pneumonia patients admitted April–October 2021. Microbiological samples were collected from 41 patients, yielding 32 culture-positive isolates (75.6%), of which 68.75% were drug-resistant organisms (predominantly Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii). Despite high rates of drug-resistant co-infection, severe comorbidities, and raised inflammatory biomarkers, the overall survival rate was 90.5% (76/84), with 8 deaths — 6 in ICU patients on mechanical ventilation and 5 associated with resistant pathogens (XDR/PDR/MDR strains), a finding reported as statistically significant (p<0.001).

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a retrospective observational microbiological profiling study — not a treatment intervention trial in the conventional sense. The 'intervention' is targeted antimicrobial therapy per culture/sensitivity results, but there is no comparison arm. Subgroup data for biomarkers (CRP, procalcitonin, D-dimer, TLC) are broken out by severity group with medians but without IQRs. Age data is reported as mean ± SD per severity subgroup (58.8±13.13 ICU/ventilated, 53.3±23.3 ICU/oxygen, 50.3±9.13 ward) but not for the overall cohort. Some figures referenced (Figures 1-4) describe resistance patterns and outcome flowcharts but quantitative data from these figures is also available in tables. Mortality in Table 5 shows 6 deaths among 32 culture-positive patients but the paper also reports 8 total deaths among 84 patients (2 culture-negative deaths in ward). Table note discrepancy: abstract states 32 (78.1%) culture-positive out of 41 samples, but results text states 31 samples positive with 32 isolates — likely 31 positive samples yielding 32 isolates (one patient had same organism from two sample types).

summary: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled 141 outpatients with subacute or chronic post-COVID cough in China and compared physician-prescribed treatment regimens (CMP capsules, ICS/LABA, Chinese patent drugs, montelukast, or combinations) to a self-selected no-medication group over 4 weeks. ICS/LABA was the most effective regimen with a 100% ORR and 89.5% complete response rate, and was independently associated with cough relief at 4 weeks in multivariate logistic regression (adjusted OR 4.42, 95% CI 1.70–13.3, p=0.004). Medicated patients showed significantly greater VAS score improvement than those who took no medication at 4 weeks (mean change 36.9 vs 21.0, p=0.025), though the lack of randomization limits causal inference.

summary: This single-center retrospective cohort study examined 42 hospitalized COVID-19 patients who developed post-COVID organizing pneumonia (OP) between March 2020 and June 2021, comparing outcomes among those treated with high-dose prednisone (60-80 mg, n=18), standard dexamethasone 6 mg (n=15), or no glucocorticoids (n=7). At discharge, the prednisone group had higher average oxygen requirements (3.5 L/min) than the dexamethasone group (2 L/min), reflecting confounding by severity; at 12-month follow-up, most patients in all groups no longer required supplemental oxygen. Mortality was highest in the high-dose prednisone group (4/18, 22%), likely reflecting baseline severity differences, with no formal statistical comparisons performed between groups.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: No formal statistical comparisons (p-values, CIs, or effect sizes) were reported between any groups; the study is purely descriptive. Baseline demographics are reported only for the overall cohort (n=42), not per arm, making confounding adjustment impossible. The 2 combination therapy patients (dexamethasone+prednisone, n=1; hydrocortisone+prednisone, n=1) are not represented as separate arms here but were included in overall counts. Treatment duration of 15.6 days is the overall average across all steroid-treated patients; per-arm duration not reported. Arm 1 n_analyzed adjusted to 17 at 12 months due to 1 lost to follow-up. summary: This prospective single-arm before-after study assessed functional and respiratory outcomes in 36 post-ICU COVID-19 survivors 3 months after discharge from an intensive inpatient multimodal rehabilitation program in Portugal. At the 3-month follow-up, patients showed significant improvements in expiratory muscle strength (MEP: 84.5 vs 97.2 cmH2O, p<0.001), peak cough flow (PCF: 367.8 vs 441.3 L/min, p=0.003), 6-minute walking distance (459 vs 500 meters, p=0.003), and sit-to-stand test repetitions (p=0.004) compared to rehabilitation discharge, while MIP, balance (Brief-BESTEST), and TUG showed no significant change. Despite overall functional gains, fatigue scores (FAS) worsened significantly at follow-up (19.0 vs 21.5, p=0.002), though values remained within the non-fatigued range.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper reports T1 (end of inpatient rehab) and T2 (3-month follow-up) but does NOT report T0 (admission) data in Table 3 — T0 data are in a prior publication (Rodrigues et al. 2022). FAS is reported as both median;IQR and mean±SD in abstract/text inconsistently: abstract states '21.50±5 vs 18.60±2.65'; table states 'median;IR' format with values 19.00;4.30 (T1) and 21.50;5.00 (T2) — the ±values in abstract appear to be IQR not SD; both median and mean/SD-equivalent values captured. summary: This single-arm retrospective cohort study evaluated ultrasound-guided stellate ganglion block (SGB) in 41 long COVID-19 patients (18 male, 23 female; symptom duration 3–29 months) treated at a Colorado pain management practice. Among the 41 patients who completed follow-up (out of 60 treated), 86% (35/41) reported reduction in at least some symptoms, and 61% (25/41) reported complete resolution of all presenting symptoms. Statistically significant pre-post improvements were observed for all 18 CDC-listed long COVID symptoms (p<0.001 for most; p<0.05 for menstrual changes), though the absence of a control group and substantial follow-up attrition limit causal inference.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Single-arm before-after study with no control group. Outcome data are binary (symptom present before SGB vs. improved/not improved after SGB) — no continuous scale scores or means/SDs. Follow-up timing was variable and not specified. Statistical tests are McNemar paired proportions tests comparing pre- vs. post-treatment symptom prevalence across all 41 patients (not just among those with a given symptom), so the 'difference in proportions' in Table 3 reflects change in prevalence across the full cohort. Rash (n=2) and fever (n=1) outcomes not extracted as separate outcome objects due to very small n but data are: rash: 2/41 pre, 2/2 (100%) relief (p<0.001 two-sided); fever: 1/41 pre, 1/1 (100%) relief (p<0.001 two-sided). Age range reported as 18–89 years but no mean/SD given. 19 patients (of 60 treated) did not respond to follow-up and are excluded from analysis — likely response bias. summary: This single-center retrospective study from Japan compared 107 long COVID patients and 222 non-long COVID patients, all presenting with chronic epipharyngitis and receiving epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT). Long COVID patients were significantly younger (median 43 vs. 40 years, p=0.018), had higher epipharyngeal endoscopic severity scores (median 5 vs. 4, p<0.001), and predominantly reported autonomic/neuroendocrine symptoms (fatigue, brain fog), while non-long COVID patients had more local inflammatory symptoms (throat discomfort, postnasal drip). extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is primarily a comparative observational study characterizing differences between long COVID and non-long COVID patients with chronic epipharyngitis; it does not report treatment outcomes (pre-post symptom scores) for EAT. Most symptom frequency data are presented only in figures (Figure 2) with p-values mentioned in text but no raw counts extractable — these were not included as separate outcome objects. Pain awareness counts in Table 1 appear to exceed the stated n (61+32=93 for n=57 long COVID; 117+82=199 for n=103 non-long COVID), suggesting these may be counts across multiple sessions rather than per-patient binary data — flagged as potentially misread. The drop-out outcomes use log-rank test p-values but actual event counts or Kaplan-Meier curves are only in Figure 4 (not extractable numerically). Overall study is descriptive/characterization rather than an efficacy trial.

summary: This retrospective cohort study compared 33 self-selected adults who received neurologic music therapy (NMT — diaphragmatic breathing, vocal intonation therapy, therapeutic singing) as an adjunct to standard inpatient rehabilitation after acute COVID-19 or PASC against 36 who declined NMT. Despite the NMT group having significantly higher oxygen requirements at baseline, both at rest and during activity, NMT participants showed significant within-group reductions in oxygen demand from admission to discharge (−0.78 L at rest, −0.85 L during activity; both p=0.003) and a significantly greater reduction in activity-based oxygen use compared to controls (Cohen's d=2.06, p=0.014). Additionally, NMT participants demonstrated significant dose-dependent improvements in sustained phonation (Pearson r=0.45 for minutes of therapy, p=0.009) and were discharged home at a significantly higher rate (97% vs. 78%, p=0.018), though no post-discharge follow-up was conducted.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1) Phonation outcome was measured only in the NMT arm (n=32 with final data; 1 participant missing discharge phonation); no comparator phonation data exists. 2) The between-group change in activity-based oxygen (outcome_id=2, timepoint null) represents the admission-to-discharge change comparison between groups (Cohen's d=2.069, p=0.014) as reported in Table 4, not a cross-sectional between-group difference at a single timepoint. 3) Days between COVID test and rehab admission differed significantly: NMT 47.3±33.0 vs non-NMT 18.9±21.3 days (p<0.001), indicating groups were not comparable at baseline — a major confounding concern. 4) Number of NMT sessions: mean 4.2±2.33 sessions; minutes mean 174±114. 5) Midpoint p-value for activity oxygen reported as <0.001, coded as p_value_exact=false. 6) The change in oxygen use from admission to discharge comparison between groups (Table 4 row: 'Change in oxygen use from rehab admission to discharge with activity') reports MD=-1.117, 95% CI -2.1126 to -0.1223, Cohen's d=2.069, p=0.014 — this is the key between-group effect for the primary outcome. 7) No subgroup analyses were conducted due to small sample size. 8) Pearson correlations (outcomes 5 and 6) reflect within-NMT-arm correlations only, not between-group effects; structure adapted accordingly.

summary: This single-arm retrospective survey-based cohort study evaluated the effect of stellate ganglion block (SGB) on PASC symptoms in 52 patients treated at a single US institution between September 2022 and September 2024. Patients received a mean of 3 SGB injections, and symptom severity was self-reported before and after treatment using a 10-point scale. Overall, 46.2% reported global improvement on a Likert scale, with the greatest median score reductions in headache (−4.5 points), brain fog, fatigue, and dizziness (all −3 points), while post-exertional malaise showed no improvement; the study had no control group and no statistical testing was performed, precluding conclusions about efficacy.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. All outcome data are medians (not means) on a 10-point scale, per stated statistical analysis methods. No SDs or IQRs were reported for individual symptom scores; figure 1 shows error bars in SD but numeric values are not given in the text or tables. The n_analyzed for each symptom outcome was inferred from the prevalence table (Table 2) as the number of patients reporting that symptom. Time between SGB and survey completion was variable and not reported systematically, making the post-SGB timepoint weeks_from_enrollment unquantifiable. The study explicitly lacked a control group and performed only descriptive statistics with no p-values. The change_mean values in within_group_change reflect median differences (not mean differences) as reported in Table 5 — this should be noted for meta-analytic use.

summary: This retrospective pre-post observational study evaluated interdisciplinary outpatient long COVID programs at two sites in Alberta, Canada (n=2,287 accepted), delivering hybrid medical and rehabilitation care over 3-6 months to adults with persistent symptoms ≥12 weeks post-infection. summary: This single-arm observational cohort study examined 61 post-COVID-19 patients undergoing 4–6 week inpatient multidisciplinary neurological rehabilitation in Germany, investigating whether baseline treatment expectations predicted outcomes. Higher side-effect expectations at baseline were significantly associated with worse outcomes at 3-month follow-up, including greater illness-related disability (PDI: β=0.42, p=0.007), reduced physical fitness on the 6MWT (β=−0.24, p=0.04), and more somatic symptoms (PHQ-15: β=0.33, p=0.006); unexpectedly, higher positive treatment expectations were associated with poorer functional status (PCFS: β=0.35, p=0.011). These associations remained significant after false discovery rate correction, suggesting that baseline expectation management may be an important target in post-COVID rehabilitation.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This study reports regression coefficients (standardized β and unstandardized B) for associations between baseline expectations and outcomes, not per-arm means/SDs at each timepoint. The paper states that means and standard deviations for outcomes are reported in Table 1 and Table 2, but these tables are not included in the text provided — only narrative results are available. No per-arm means or SDs could be extracted for any outcome at any timepoint. The study is single-arm (no comparison group), so between_group_effects are not applicable. Positive treatment expectations mean=6.22 (scale 0–10); negative treatment expectations mean=0.82; side-effect expectations mean=1.63 at baseline. Rehabilitation duration was 4–6 weeks (mean 32 days in inpatient stay). The primary analyses are regression associations between baseline expectations and outcomes, not pre-post efficacy estimates — this is fundamentally an expectation/placebo mechanisms study, not a treatment efficacy trial. Duration unit set to weeks with value 4 as lower bound (range 4–6 weeks); total follow-up calculated as ~5 weeks treatment + 12 weeks post-treatment = ~17 weeks.

summary: This prospective single-center cohort study in China compared TCM syndrome-differentiation treatment (CRPRF or YTRF herbal decoctions; n=1204) versus standard Western symptomatic medicine (n=202) in 1426 long COVID patients over a 90-day follow-up. The TCM group had a shorter mean time to symptom improvement (12.28±6.98 vs 14.61±9.93 days) and a higher symptom improvement rate (90.65% vs 80.68%), with significantly greater improvements in TCM syndrome scores and in specific symptoms including insomnia, fatigue, shortness of breath, sore throat, and aversion to cold (all p<0.05). summary: This prospective observational cohort study assessed fat oxidation (FatOx) capacity via CPET breath-by-breath spirometry in 187 long COVID (PCS) patients before and after ~4 weeks of inpatient exercise-based rehabilitation in Germany. Exercise-based rehabilitation produced a statistically significant ~32% improvement in overall FatOx AUC (from 11.3 to 14.9, p=0.0025), with the greatest gain (~45%) seen in a predominantly younger male subgroup with the most severely restricted baseline FatOx, suggesting exercise rehabilitation can restore mitochondrial fat oxidation capacity in long COVID.

summary: This uncontrolled single-arm pilot study evaluated intranasal photobiomodulation (808 nm laser, 60 J/session) for anosmia and intraoral dual-wavelength photobiomodulation (660 nm + 808 nm, 216 J/session) for ageusia in 20 post-COVID-19 patients with persistent smell and taste loss (≥3 months duration), treated over 12 sessions across approximately 4 weeks. summary: This open-label pilot study randomized 14 adults with long COVID brain fog (≥5 months post-acute cognitive decline) to 12 sessions of either transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM; 1070 nm helmet, n=7) or whole-body photobiomodulation (wbPBM; 660/850 nm light bed, n=7) over 4 weeks. summary: This single-arm prospective cohort study evaluated a 6-week WHO Borg CR-10 structured pacing protocol in 31 adults with long-standing post-COVID syndrome (median symptom duration 17 months) attending a community rehabilitation service in the UK. The primary outcome, total weekly PESE episodes, decreased significantly from a mean of 3.4 in Week 1 to 1.1 in Week 6, representing an average 16% reduction per week (95% CI: 9%-24%; p<0.001), with improvements across physical, cognitive, and emotional exertion triggers. Quality of life (EQ-5D VAS) also improved significantly from 51.4 to 60.6 points (paired difference 9.2 points, 95% CI: 3.2-15.2; p=0.004), though the absence of a control group limits causal inference.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a single-arm pre-post study (no randomization, no control group); the study_design RCT schema does not fully apply. Rate ratios for weekly change were back-calculated from reported percentage decreases (e.g., 16% decrease = rate ratio 0.84). The 95% CIs for cognitive dysfunction symptom trajectory (-12% to 16%) indicate the lower CI is -0.12, upper 0.16 relative to the rate, so rate_ratio CI is 0.88 to 1.16. Some per-arm SDs for PESE episode counts not reported. Data for duration of PESE episodes over time appears primarily in Figure 4 with limited textual data. The n=34 consented but n=31 analyzed; the 3 excluded did not complete the full 6 weeks. The study notes 4 participants 'could not comply' but 3 were excluded from analysis - slight ambiguity in reporting. Weekly episode counts by trigger type (physical, cognitive, emotional) reported only as frequencies in Figure 2, not as per-week means in table format.

summary: This single-arm pre-post intervention study evaluated individualized stress-controlled training therapy (Blended Therapy: computerized system + home exercises) followed by intensified cognitive behavioral therapy in 78 vaccinated long COVID patients with fatigue and sensorimotor instability at the Post-COVID-19 Center Lausitz, Germany, over 3 years (2021–2023). summary: This single-arm pre-post study evaluated low dose naltrexone (LDN; 1 mg/day escalating to 2 mg/day over 2 months) in 52 patients with long COVID (median symptom duration 333 days) at a single Irish tertiary hospital. Among the 36 participants who completed follow-up questionnaires, significant improvements were observed in 6 of 7 Likert-scale outcomes including pain (largest effect size r=0.534), recovery from COVID-19, activities of daily living, energy, concentration, and sleep (all p≤0.001); mood improvement was not statistically significant (p=0.054). The study lacked a control arm, so improvements cannot be attributed solely to LDN versus placebo effect or natural recovery, but LDN appeared safe with only 2 of 38 participants (5.3%) discontinuing due to adverse events.

summary: This single-arm open diagnostic study enrolled 30 long COVID patients (median age 41, 73% female) with symptoms persisting ≥6 months, assessing airflow limitation via methacholine bronchial provocation test and app-based diurnal FEV1 variability monitoring, followed by 3 weeks of inhaled corticosteroid-based asthma treatment. Airflow limitation was detected in 29/30 patients (97%), either by positive methacholine BPT (8/30, 27%) or excessive diurnal FEV1 variability (21/22 BPT-negative patients, 95%). Three weeks of asthma treatment significantly normalized mean diurnal FEV1 variability from 18.0% to 7.3% (p<0.001), eliminated dyspnoea (3.0 to 0, p<0.001), and significantly reduced fatigue scores (8.3 to 6.1, p<0.001), suggesting that unrecognized airflow limitation may contribute to long COVID symptoms and respond to asthma therapy.

summary: This single-arm pilot study administered a 6-week course of oral minocycline (200mg loading then 100mg/day) to 55 patients with ME/CFS, including 19 with long COVID, at a single Japanese clinic. Among the 51 who completed treatment, 80% achieved a clinically meaningful improvement in Performance Status score (>=2 point decrease), with particularly high response rates in those with disease duration <6 months (90%; HR 3.6, p=0.02). Statistically significant improvements were observed in fatigue, post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, brain fog, orthostatic intolerance, and disequilibrium, but the study lacks a control group, blinding, or randomization, making placebo effects and natural disease course impossible to exclude.

summary: This single-arm interventional cohort study tested Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy (PSRT) — a 13-week program combining psychophysiologic education, desensitization, and mindfulness-based stress reduction — in 23 adults with long COVID (PASC) without organ injury who had experienced symptoms for a median of 267 days. summary: This single-arm exploratory study treated 95 Dutch post-COVID syndrome (PCS) patients with SSRIs (primarily citalopram, venlafaxine, and fluvoxamine) for at least 4-6 weeks, measuring outcomes with three instruments: a rated open-question, a symptom severity score list, and the Bell Functionality Score. Two-thirds of patients (63.4%) reported reasonably good to strong improvement in symptoms, with brainfog and sensory overload showing the greatest reduction (3.8 and 3.6 points on a 10-point scale), and Bell scores improving from 23.5 to 47.2 (BF = 9.6×10^17). As an uncontrolled pre-post study without randomization or a control group, placebo effects and natural recovery cannot be excluded, but the delayed response onset and sustained benefit are offered as partial evidence against a pure placebo explanation.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is NOT an RCT — it is a single-arm observational pre-post cohort study with no control group and no randomization. The study design fields have been populated accordingly. Per-arm means and SDs are not available for individual symptom score list outcomes at baseline or follow-up; only mean change scores are reported for brainfog (-3.8), sensory overload (-3.6), muscle pain (-2.1), and muscle weakness (-1.9) from figures/text. No exact change scores were reported in text for chronic fatigue, headache, dyspnea, or palpitations — these are visible only in Fig. 3 violin plots and could not be extracted numerically. Bell score means are available (94.2 pre-Covid, 23.5 during PCS baseline, 47.2 after SSRI) but SDs are not reported in text. Bayesian statistics (Bayes Factors) are used throughout rather than traditional p-values and CIs; no confidence intervals are reported for any outcome. The garbled characters in the paper title and text (e.g. 'ͷ9' representing numbers, 'ͷͶ%' for 10%) reflect Unicode encoding issues in the source PDF — values have been interpreted from context. The paper title reads '95 post-Covid patients' and the 10% no-response figure is confirmed by n=9/95.
